MFL lineups are a starter total plus a min–max range per position, not slots. This league (QB 1-2, RB 0-4, WR 0-5, TE 1-3, PK 1, DT+DE 1-3, LB 1-3, CB+S 1-3; 14 starters, 5 of them IDP) can't be expressed exactly as SlotDef[] — offense: 4 position range(s) cap the 6 flex spots (QB ≤ 1 extra, RB ≤ 4 extra, WR ≤ 5 extra, TE ≤ 2 extra) and their caps add up to 12 > 6, which no SlotDef set can express; SlotDefs alone over-allow them, so the solver needs starterCaps (evidence B.flex). Options: (a) add optional per-position starter caps (min/max) to LeagueSettings and solve lineups with a flow network that honours them; (b) approximate with SlotDefs and warn on the Import Report.

MFL roster limits carry minimums as well as maximums (QB ≥ 1, RB ≥ 1, WR ≥ 1, TE ≥ 1, K ≥ 1, DL ≥ 1, LB ≥ 1, DB ≥ 1) but CLAUDE.md §4 positionLimits holds maximums only — evidence B.positionLimits (GET https://{leagueHost}/2026/export?TYPE=league&L={leagueId}&JSON=1 → HTTP 200, league.rosterLimits.position[].limit) — options: (a) add optional positionMinimums and make auto-drops respect them; (b) ignore minimums (a trade could leave a roster illegal on MFL) and warn on the trade card.

The rule compiler adds up rules from overlapping MFL position groups (e.g. "QB|RB|WR|TE" plus "TE"), as MFL's scoring help describes, but this league has no overlapping groups (C.receptions), so the 100% oracle does not validate that path — options: re-run the oracle on an MFL league with overlapping groups in Phase 5 before relying on it.

MFL range rules don't all fit the Scoring model: per-unit rates that apply only inside a range (tiered), stepped "a/b" awards (floor — "1 pt every 10 yds" gives 12 for 128 yds) and formula rules (thresholdPoints). This league: 0 tiered/formula rule-position pair(s) unmapped, 0 stepped pair(s) approximated as linear, 1 formula pair(s) that still compile exactly (evidence C.mapping). Options: (a) extend Scoring with generic range rules {stat, min, max, kind: each|every|flat|formula, points, per} evaluated as expected values like bonuses; (b) approximate and list them in scoring.unmapped.

Owner display names aren't returned to a guest (§17 D): league.franchises.franchise[] has only ["abbrev","division","icon","id","logo","name","stadium","waiverSortOrder"] — evidence D.owners (GET https://{leagueHost}/2026/export?TYPE=league&L={leagueId}&JSON=1 → HTTP 200) — options: (a) with an owner login, read owner_name (untested); (b) show team names only on the Import Report and trade cards for public MFL leagues.

MFL gives expected return dates: 66 of 66 rostered injured players have injuries.injury[].exp_return, 57 of them inside the 2026 season — CLAUDE.md §6 assumes platforms rarely give a return week and falls back to fixed injury tables (evidence E.injury, GET https://api.myfantasyleague.com/2026/export?TYPE=injuries&JSON=1 → HTTP 200) — options: (a) use exp_return as injuryReturnWeek for MFL leagues (recommended; the date → week mapping uses NFL kickoff times); (b) ignore it and keep the §6 defaults.

TYPE=schedule marks unplayed matchups as ties: 110 franchise-weeks after CompletedWeek 3 carry result "T" (F.futureResult; GET https://{leagueHost}/2026/export?TYPE=schedule&L={leagueId}&JSON=1 → HTTP 200) — options: count results only for weeks ≤ mfl_status CompletedWeek (recommended; the probe's standings cross-check does this and matches 10/10 teams).

MFL transactions have no week field (unix timestamps only) and include types the TRANS_TYPE docs don't list (AUTO_PROCESS_WAIVERS ×2, LOAD_ROSTERS ×27, LOCK_ALL_PLAYERS ×3; documented: WAIVER, BBID_WAIVER, FREE_AGENT, WAIVER_REQUEST, BBID_WAIVER_REQUEST, TRADE, IR, TAXI, AUCTION_INIT, AUCTION_BID, AUCTION_WON, SURVIVOR_PICK, POOL_PICK) — evidence G.addDrop / G.week (GET https://{leagueHost}/2026/export?TYPE=transactions&L={leagueId}&TRANS_TYPE=*&JSON=1 → HTTP 200) — options: derive the week as MFL's W= filter does (the next week to kick off; lib/mfl/derive.ts nextKickoffWeek, checked against MFL in G.week) and keep moves before the first kickoff apart as preseason (txWeek); treat unknown types as non-roster events and list them in the Import Report warnings.

MFL has no Sleeper ids (TYPE=players DETAILS=1 carries no sleeper_id): canonical ids need the DynastyProcess crosswalk (mfl_id→sleeper_id) plus ID joins through the Sleeper players DB — 383/383 rostered players matched (X.crosswalk); league-specific custom player ids (14 here) come back only from TYPE=players with L= and 2 of them collide with DynastyProcess rows for other players, so they must never be crosswalked — options: (a) DynastyProcess first, then Sleeper-DB ID joins (implemented in lib/mfl/oracle.ts); (b) treat custom players as league-only players with no projections or market value.

MFL's league-scored projections and Sleeper's stat projections × this league's rules disagree systematically: median MFL ÷ Sleeper×rules = 0.812 in week 4 (n=179; 12 players differ by > 40%) — evidence J.agreement (GET https://{leagueHost}/2026/export?TYPE=projectedScores&L={leagueId}&W=4&JSON=1 → HTTP 200; GET https://api.sleeper.app/projections/nfl/2026/4?season_type=regular&position={position} → HTTP 200). §6 averages the two sources for MFL leagues, which shifts MFL players' base rates by about half that gap and logs every > 40% disagreement — options: (a) average as specified and log the disagreements; (b) rescale MFL projections to Sleeper's level (or tune a per-source weight) in the Phase 6 backtest before averaging; (c) use Sleeper × league rules only, like the other platforms.

MFL never publishes raw stats (K.rawStats; api_info), so the §5 scoring oracle for MFL recomputes playerScores from Sleeper's undocumented /stats endpoint joined by the crosswalk: 604/604 rostered player-weeks within 0.05 in weeks 2–3 (K.oracle; skipped {"noCrosswalk":28,"noCompiledScoring":0,"bothZero":162}) — options: keep Sleeper stats as the MFL oracle source (recommended while the endpoint works); fall back to nflverse weekly stats if it breaks.

§17 M target missed for this MFL league: 258/268 = 96.3% of rostered QB/RB/WR/TE have a FantasyCalc value row by mflId (target ≥ 98%); 10 of the 10 misses are in FantasyCalc's /players list, i.e. they exist but have no value in this format (isDynasty=true&numQbs=2&numTeams=10&ppr=0.5) — evidence M.matchRate — options: (a) count ID-level coverage (100.0%) and give value-less players config.valueFloor (as §9 already says); (b) keep the 98% target on value rows and accept deep-bench misses.

CLAUDE.md §2.6 lists TYPE=standings, but api_info?STATE=details doesn't document it; the live server still answers it (HTTP 200, root keys ["encoding","leagueStandings","version"]) — evidence X.standingsAlias (GET https://{leagueHost}/2026/export?TYPE=standings&L={leagueId}&JSON=1) — options: use the documented TYPE=leagueStandings (recommended); keep "standings" only as an undocumented alias.

CLAUDE.md §2.6 says "Follow redirects to the league's wwwNN host", but (1) api_info warns a wrong-host redirect "may be delayed, or if the system is under too much stress, it may be denied", (2) this run's api-host league request was redirected (HTTP 302), and (3) Node's fetch drops the Cookie header on a cross-host redirect, so a private league would silently answer as a guest — evidence X.redirect, DOCS.hosts — options: (a) send league requests to league.baseURL's host (implemented); (b) follow redirects by hand, re-attaching the cookie only for https *.myfantasyleague.com (implemented in lib/mfl/client.ts; offline-tested, untested live: no MFL login).

MFL reports errors as HTTP 200 with an "error" object (like §2.7 says for Fantrax; §2.6 doesn't mention it): TYPE=calendar as a guest → HTTP 200, body error "API requires logged in user in league ID 10001 - Please be sure to pass the proper MFL_USER_ID cookie or APIKEY parameter" — evidence A.tradeDeadline — options: treat any MFL body with an "error" key as a failure and never cache it (implemented in lib/mfl/client.ts).

CLAUDE.md §0.9 says to back off exponentially on 429/5xx, but api_info says "If a request fails, don't retry" and "Wait one second between making requests" (DOCS.rate) — the probe follows MFL for MFL hosts (no retries; a 429 stops MFL calls for the run) — options: (a) keep MFL's rule as a documented exception to §0.9 (recommended); (b) allow one delayed retry on 5xx only.
decisions: FantasyCalc format for this league: isDynasty=true (assumed from the A.leagueType signals: dynasty), numQbs=2 (QB range allows 2 starters), numTeams=10, ppr=0.5; the TE premium (TE 1 per catch) is not passed — the tep parameter is still unverified (shared probe).

League requests go to the league's own host (league.baseURL for MFL_LEAGUE_ID, the search hit's homeURL for the test league); non-league TYPEs to api.myfantasyleague.com — as api_info asks. Redirects are followed by hand (redirect: "manual") and only to https *.myfantasyleague.com, so a login cookie survives an api → wwwNN hop.

Pacing: every *.myfantasyleague.com request (api host, league hosts, docs pages, redirect hops) shares one bucket in lib/http.ts, ≥ 1.2 s apart; retries: 0 on every MFL request; one 429 stops further MFL calls for the run (api_info: "If a request fails, don't retry").

Cache: league data 10 min, league-scored projections 6 h, players DB 24 h (api_info: "no more than once per day"), allRules 7 days, docs pages 7 days (HTML cached on purpose), NFL schedule/byes 7 days, injuries 6 h, the leagueSearch result 24 h plus the saved test-league choice; MFL HTTP-200 error bodies are never cached.
Private leagues: log in with MFL_USERNAME/MFL_PASSWORD via POST and send the MFL_USER_ID cookie; the APIKEY alternative is not used because it travels in the URL query string.

Test league (MFL_LEAGUE_ID blank): one public TYPE=leagueSearch, then a few candidates in a random order keyed by a salt that lives only in the git-ignored choice file, until a public, in-season 10–12 team league with IR and taxi slots in use (this one: dynasty); the IDs and names of the leagues looked at go to the git-ignored watch list for check:leaks.

MFL responses are put in canonical order (sorted keys; id-keyed arrays sorted — lib/mfl/canonical.ts) before identities are registered and fixtures saved, so placeholders and committed fixtures stay stable run to run; fixtures/raw keeps MFL's exact bytes.

Scoring semantics taken from MFL's Scoring Rules Setup help: *N per unit, a/b stepped every-b, plain N flat award in range, thresholdPoints = formula scoring; rules in overlapping position groups add up. lib/mfl/rules.ts compiles them to Sleeper-key rates + stat ≥ threshold bonuses and reports what doesn't fit.
questions: Do you have an MFL league? If so, fill in MFL_LEAGUE_ID (and MFL_USERNAME + MFL_PASSWORD if it's private) in .env.local.
Should we register an MFL API client (needs your MFL account and an SMS code) for ~2.5× higher rate limits before launch? Not needed for development.
MFL lineups use min–max ranges per position: OK to add optional per-position starter caps to LeagueSettings (Phase 5) instead of approximating with flex slots?
OK to follow MFL's own "don't retry" rule for MFL hosts as an exception to §0.9's exponential backoff?
